title: The gate between an unreviewed hardware claim and evidence
note: R51 said the scientific tree had no mutation coverage at all, and this is the part of it that matters most: hardware_governance_3d.py decides whether a measurement record counts as reviewed evidence, and PASS staying at zero is exactly the claim that rests on it. H1-H4 attack the intake boundary -- a record that fails its schema must be REJECTED rather than quarantined, and a quarantined record must never acquire evidentiary standing. H5-H9 attack the review binding, which is the confused-deputy surface here: a review must be authored by a human, must decide ACCEPT_AS_EVIDENCE explicitly, and must bind to THIS record by digest rather than merely naming its id, or a reviewed record can be swapped for an unreviewed one after the fact. H10-H11 attack the two constants a reader takes at face value: automatic_gate_effect NONE and can_PASS_now NO. H12-H21 were added with D-2026-42, which found that all of the above ran on top of a reviewer identity that resolved to nothing: H6 killed a review that CONFESSED to being tool-authored, and a program that simply omitted the flag authored a review that admitted a record into a dossier. These attack the resolution itself -- the kind, the chain of trust back to the out-of-band bootstrap, retirement, exact naming, and the two request-side identities -- plus the count the dossier reports about its own authority.

mutations.find: AUTOMATIC_GATE_EFFECT = "NONE"
mutations.rationale: every report in this module states automatic_gate_effect, and NONE is the sentence that keeps an unreviewed hardware claim from moving a gate on its own. A reader takes it at face value

mutations.rationale: case-insensitive resolution makes two spellings one subject, which defeats the requester/reviewer separation from the other side: the requester respells themselves into the reviewer list and the identity check agrees

mutations.name: H18_a_matrix_update_request_never_resolves_its_reviewers
mutations.find:

mutations.rationale: review_ids go back to being strings nobody looks up, so a request citing reviews that do not exist validates -- reproduced with two invented ids before D-2026-42

mutations.name: H19_a_matrix_update_request_never_resolves_its_requester
mutations.find:
_, why_req = resolve_reviewer(doc["requester"], roster,
                                  at=doc.get("request_date"))
    reasons += [f"requester: {w}" for w in why_req]
mutations.rationale: any string may propose a validation-matrix status change, which is the authority the request document exists to carry

mutations.name: H20_a_roster_that_cannot_name_one_subject_is_used_anyway

        return None, list(roster["problems"])
mutations.rationale: a roster holding two ids that differ only in case, or the same id twice, is resolved against instead of refused; the naming authority stops being able to say which subject a review means and answers anyway

mutations.name: H21_the_dossier_does_not_say_which_authority_decided_it
mutations.find: "n_registered_reviewers": len(roster.get("reviewers") or {}),
mutations.rationale: the dossier reports a reviewer count it did not measure, so an empty dossier can no longer be read as 'nobody is registered' rather than 'every record was deficient' -- the anti-vacuity statement becomes a constant

suites_note: H17-H19 SURVIVED on the first run of the extended spec, and the harness says what to check before recording that as a missing test: whether a suite outside this list already covers it. It did. validate_matrix_update_request and the reviewer resolution it calls are exercised from tests/test_stage6_roadmap.py and tests/test_stage7_boundary.py, and tests/test_review_binding.py holds the review-to-record binding this spec also mutates. The spec was mis-scoped -- it named the module's intake and dossier suites and mutated its request path too -- and a mis-scoped spec and a missing test look identical from inside the harness. Recorded rather than fixed silently, because 'SURVIVED' was the correct output and the wrong conclusion.
